title: Shared primitive types
description: Identifiers, causal paths, timestamps and versions shared by every OpenEngine V2 contract. Every identifier is a single NATS subject token: it never contains '.', '*', '>' or whitespace, so it can be placed in a subject without escaping. Resource identifiers carry a type prefix so an identifier placed in the wrong slot is rejected.

token.description: A single NATS subject token: ASCII letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit, at most 128 characters.

command_id.description: Instance-wide identity of a logical command, chosen by the sender and reused unchanged on every retry. Any subject token; `cmd_` is the conventional prefix.

event_id.description: Stable identity of an event, reused unchanged when the event is republished. Also sent as the `Nats-Msg-Id` header so the stream deduplicates republication.

request_id.description: Caller-chosen diagnostic identifier for a query. Not used for routing.

causal_id.description: One element of a causal path: a command ID, an event ID, or a scoped external root ID such as `gh-conn_7-delivery_4411`.

causal_path.description: Primary causal ancestry, root first, ending with the ID of the message that carries it. At most 32 elements, no repeats. A message whose path would exceed 32 elements is not sent and its operation fails with CAUSAL_PATH_TOO_LONG; paths are never truncated.

utc_timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, written with a trailing 'Z'.

resource_version.description: Monotonic version of a resource, starting at 1 and incremented by every accepted change.

slug.description: Lower-case machine name, such as a provider or agent name.

producer.description: Logical service that emitted a message.

resource_name.description: A namespace or the name of a namespaced resource, such as a Tool or a ToolInvocation: lower-case letters, digits and `-`, starting and ending with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters. It has no type prefix; the subject's position says what it names.

execution_id.description: A graph execution: one run of a graph revision within a job.

step_instance_id.description: One entry into a graph node within a graph execution.

step_attempt_id.description: One try at a step instance. A retried step has several attempts.

workflow_approval_id.description: A GE-owned approval gate in a graph execution.

workspace_id.description: Stable workspace identity. Survives suspension, restoration and runtime replacement.

runtime_id.description: One provisioned compute runtime backing a workspace. Restoration after suspension creates a new runtime.

runtime_generation.description: Counter incremented every time a workspace receives a new runtime. Runtime approvals and sessions are bound to the generation that created them.

session_id.description: An agent conversation inside a workspace. A session can span several task attempts.

attempt_id.description: One task attempt started by `execute`: the unit VCP cancels.

runtime_approval_id.description: A VCP-owned approval raised by an agent runtime inside a workspace.

message_id.description: A conversation message within a session.

resource_refs.description: Typed references to the resources a message concerns, keyed by identifier name. Service schemas narrow this to the exact keys each message requires.

traceparent.description: W3C Trace Context `traceparent` header (`{version}-{trace-id}-{parent-id}-{trace-flags}`), lower-case hex. Names the span that sent the message, so the receiver's work joins the sender's trace.

tracestate.description: W3C Trace Context `tracestate` header: vendor-specific trace data carried alongside `traceparent`, passed on unchanged.

trace_headers.description: Optional W3C Trace Context headers. Every request and event may carry them; a receiver that gets none starts a new trace.
